root_cause.text: KVM's SEV/SEV-ES VMSA synchronization path in sev_es_sync_vmsa() failed to check whether the vCPU's VMSA had already been launched/encrypted, allowing the kernel to write to guest-private encrypted VMSA memory after launch.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds an early guard `if (vcpu->arch.guest_state_protected) return -EINVAL;` to `sev_es_sync_vmsa()`, and the commit/CVE explicitly state that syncing an already-launched/encrypted VMSA causes host access to guest-private memory and an SNP RMP page fault in `sev_es_sync_vmsa`.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch adds an early guard `if (vcpu->arch.guest_state_protected) return -EINVAL;` to `sev_es_sync_vmsa()`, and the commit/CVE explicitly state that syncing an already-launched/encrypted VMSA causes host access to guest-private memory and an SNP RMP page fault in `sev_es_sync_vmsa`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a guard in sev_es_sync_vmsa() to reject VMSA synchronization when the guest state is already protected.
intent_record.what: A new early-return check was added at the start of sev_es_sync_vmsa() that tests vcpu->arch.guest_state_protected and returns -EINVAL when it is true, before the existing debug-field validation logic.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now refuses to synchronize the VMSA for a vCPU whose guest state is already marked as protected, preventing the rest of the VMSA encryption/sync path from running in that state and rejecting the operation with an invalid-argument error.

grouping_result.intent: Add a guard in sev_es_sync_vmsa() to reject VMSA synchronization when the guest state is already protected.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly adds the missing check in sev_es_sync_vmsa() to prevent syncing/writing the VMSA after it has been launched/protected, which matches the stated root cause.

candidates.rationale: This pre-existing guard checked only debug-related conditions before VMSA synchronization/encryption, but omitted any check for whether the VMSA had already been launched/encrypted. That missing state validation is the direct root cause enabling writes to guest-private encrypted VMSA memory after launch.

vuln_statements.explanation: This was the only pre-synchronization guard shown in sev_es_sync_vmsa(). It validated debug-related state but failed to also reject synchronization when the VMSA had already been launched/encrypted, which is the root cause that allowed writes to guest-private encrypted VMSA memory after launch.

bic_trace_step.reason: The function body of `sev_es_sync_vmsa()` is sufficient to decide because it shows the full VMSA synchronization logic. The root cause is absence of a check that the VMSA has already been launched/encrypted before writing to it. In this snippet, `save` is set to `svm->sev_es.vmsa` (`struct sev_es_save_area *save = svm->sev_es.vmsa;`), and the function then writes directly into that buffer. It first does `memcpy(save, &svm->vmcb->save, sizeof(svm->vmcb->save));` and then continues with many field assignments such as `save->rax = ...`, `save->rbx = ...`, etc. The only guard present is `if (svm->vcpu.guest_debug || (svm->vmcb->save.dr7 & ~DR7_FIXED_1)) return -EINVAL;`, which is only a debug/DR7 validation and not a launch/encryption state check. There is no condition checking whether the VMSA has already been launched or is guest-private encrypted before performing the writes. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present, and the fix is not present in this function.

bic_trace_step.reason: The diff provides the full body of the relevant function `sev_es_sync_vmsa()` and its caller `sev_launch_update_vmsa()`, which is sufficient to judge the presence of the vulnerable logic. In `sev_es_sync_vmsa()`, the code unconditionally writes register state into the VMSA-backed memory: `save->rax = ...`, `save->rbx = ...`, ... `save->rip = ...`, then copies the VMCB save area into the SEV-ES VMSA page with `memcpy(svm->vmsa, save, sizeof(*save));`. There is no check anywhere in this function to determine whether the VMSA has already been launched/encrypted/protected before writing to `svm->vmsa`. The caller `sev_launch_update_vmsa()` then encrypts that same page in place via `SEV_CMD_LAUNCH_UPDATE_VMSA` and marks the vCPU as protected only afterward with `svm->vcpu.arch.guest_state_protected = true;`. The root cause states that the bug is failure to check whether the vCPU's VMSA had already been launched/encrypted before synchronizing, allowing writes to guest-private encrypted VMSA memory after launch. This commit introduces the sync path but does not contain any guard such as checking `guest_state_protected` before performing the writes/copy, so the vulnerable construct is present and the fix is not present.
